clue.text: Jewel to the fore in Eastern hairdressing

blocks.note: a brilliant is a diamond cut with many facets
taken as written
E is the standard abbreviation for Eastern

explanation.surface: An Eastern hairstyle shows off a jewel at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To the fore' just tells you the jewel comes first, followed by the other pieces in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliantine is a scented oil once used to make men's hair glossy, so it is a hairdressing product.

clue.text: Comic strip hero protecting old Charon, say

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding something to guard it

blocks.note: the caped crusader of DC comics
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A comic-strip superhero shields the ancient ferryman Charon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks Charon as an example: in Greek myth he rows the dead across the river Styx.
explanation.definitionFit: Charon ferries souls in a boat, so he is a mythological example of someone who rows boats for hire.

clue.text: Bring on fashionable dog

blocks.note: in means in fashion
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Fetch out the trendy dog.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a penalty or cost is to bring it upon yourself.

clue.text: Appear keen to bestir oneself

blocks.note: first meaning: literally, seem sharp or alert
second meaning: the idiom urging someone to hurry up

explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning takes the phrase word by word; the second is the everyday command to get moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Look means appear and sharp means keen, while the set phrase is a command to hurry and get moving.

clue.text: A fish in jelly

blocks.note: taken as written
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A fish is set in aspic.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a gelatinous substance made from seaweed, used to set food and culture bacteria.

clue.text: He's in tap-dancing-it's dramatic

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and end up in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer tap-dances, and it makes for a theatrical show.
explanation.walkthrough: The word works as an adjective here as well as the usual noun for an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: From Thespis, the legendary first Greek actor, the adjective means relating to drama or the theatre.

clue.text: Ravine everyone in France climbs

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means reading from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: split as every plus one: every is all, and one in French is un

explanation.surface: Everybody in France scrambles up a gorge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Everyone' must be split into every and one.
explanation.definitionFit: A nulla or nullah is an Anglo-Indian word for a dry watercourse or steep gully.

clue.text: Not the island with a lake — that's imaginary

blocks.note: taken as written
Iona is the Hebridean island where St Columba founded his monastery
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Not the island with a loch — that one does not exist.
explanation.walkthrough: Iona is a small island off the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Notional means existing only as an idea in the mind rather than in reality.

clue.text: Uptight about the church's hypocrisy

indicators.note: about means going round something else

blocks.note: read as up plus tight: tight is tied, fastened firmly, and up (in a down clue) says to read the result from the bottom
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A tense person complains about the hypocrisy of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uptight' is split into up and tight; the church goes inside before the whole is turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceit is deliberate misleading, and hypocrisy is the deceit of pretending to virtues one lacks.

clue.text: Roads in Alaska

blocks.note: first meaning: a sheltered stretch of water where ships lie at anchor, also called roads or a roadstead
second meaning: the largest city of the state of Alaska

explanation.walkthrough: 'Roads' looks like highways, but in nautical language roads are a safe place for ships to moor offshore.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadstead where vessels moor is an anchorage, and Anchorage is also the chief port city in that northern American state.

clue.text: Anita has a point, being unattached

blocks.note: Anita Loos was the American author of Gentlemen Prefer Blondes
a point of the compass, here East

explanation.surface: A woman called Anita makes a fair argument about being single.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Anita's dating status; really she is the writer Anita Loos, and 'has' joins her surname to a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unattached is not fastened or tied down, which is exactly what loose means.

clue.text: Girl on an instant becoming sullen

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, as in 'half a mo'
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman suddenly turns sulky.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' places the girl after the instant.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose describes a gloomy, sulky, ill-humoured temper, a close synonym of sullen.

clue.text: In a mood to veto a pit, perhaps

definitions.note: adjectival: said of a verb in the mood expressing a wish

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters given are only one possible ordering, so try others

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is in a bad temper and minded to block plans for a mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a mood' reads as being grumpy; in grammar a mood is a verb form such as the indicative or subjunctive.
explanation.definitionFit: The optative is a grammatical verb mood expressing wishes, found in Greek and Sanskrit.

clue.text: No end of impudence given by sailor in drink

indicators.note: with no end, the final letter of the word for cheek is dropped

blocks.note: neck means cheek or nerve in British slang
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A cheeky sailor is endlessly insolent while drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar was the drink of the Greek gods, and is used for any delicious drink.

clue.text: Money finds general acceptance

blocks.note: first meaning: the coins and notes used in a country
second meaning: as when an idea gains wide circulation

explanation.walkthrough: An idea that has currency is widely accepted or believed.
explanation.definitionFit: Currency is a nation's system of cash, and also the state of being widely circulated or believed.

clue.text: Jewelled collar, secret in weight

indicators.note: in places one item inside another

blocks.note: ct is the abbreviation for carat, the jeweller's weight
arcane means known only to a few

explanation.surface: A jewelled collar hides a secret in how heavy it is.
explanation.definitionFit: A carcanet is an archaic word for an ornamental necklace or collar set with jewels.

clue.text: Queen is in the palace to change

definitions.text: Queen is in the palace to change

indicators.note: is in places one item inside a group of others
change tells you to alter the order of the preceding letters

blocks.note: R is short for Regina, Latin for queen
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The queen is in her palace, ready to dress.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a picture of the famous Egyptian queen at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra was the last ruling queen of Ptolemaic Egypt, who lived in a royal palace at Alexandria.

clue.text: Thrill to introduce rock in cheap joint

indicators.note: to introduce means to put something inside

blocks.note: to send someone is to thrill them
a crag is a steep rock face

explanation.surface: A thrilling chance to bring rock music into a seedy club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like a bar or club, but it is a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: The scrag end is the bony neck of mutton, an inexpensive cut of meat for stews.

clue.text: Fish — one out of a shell

indicators.note: out of is read as being outside, so one part wraps round the other

blocks.note: a carp is a freshwater fish
taken as written
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A lone fish has been taken out of its shell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of' looks like removal; here it means the fish sits outside the A, with the one following.
explanation.definitionFit: A carapace is the hard upper shell of a tortoise, crab or lobster.

clue.text: Dramatist's business tie-up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
a tie in a game is a draw

explanation.surface: A playwright's company forms a merger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tie-up' looks like a business partnership; it splits into tie and up.
explanation.definitionFit: Noël Coward was an English playwright, author of Private Lives and Blithe Spirit.

clue.text: Beauties Betjeman said he was summoned by

indicators.note: said points to a word spoken rather than spelt

blocks.clueFragment: Betjeman said he was summoned by
blocks.note: John Betjeman's verse autobiography is called Summoned by Bells

explanation.surface: Poet John Betjeman claimed pretty women were calling him.
explanation.walkthrough: Betjeman was a Poet Laureate; his memoir in verse is titled Summoned by Bells, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Belles are beautiful women, from the French word for beautiful.

clue.text: Sprig of flowers on Queen Elizabeth rose

blocks.note: a spray is a small branch with flowers
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A spray of flowers features a Queen Elizabeth rose, a famous variety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like the flower or a past tense; it is the perforated nozzle of a watering can.
explanation.definitionFit: The rose on a watering can or hose is the perforated head that sprays water, so it is a sprayer.

clue.text: Bird to weather a storm

indicators.note: a storm throws things about, so the letters are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird has to ride out a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weather a storm' is a familiar phrase, which hides that 'storm' is the signal acting on the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheatear is a small migratory songbird with a white rump, seen on open moorland.

clue.text: Student approach upsetting — a sort of wave

indicators.note: upsetting turns something over, so in a down clue it is read upwards

blocks.note: L is a learner driver
an adit is a horizontal entrance to a mine

explanation.surface: A student's approach is upsetting and causes a ripple.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidal describes a tidal wave, so the adjective names one kind of wave.

clue.text: In Egypt, a vote for trouble

indicators.note: In puts one thing inside another

blocks.note: the United Arab Republic, Egypt's official name from 1958 to 1971
a vote in favour is a pro

explanation.surface: An Egyptian election produces a vote for unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: Egypt kept the name United Arab Republic after its union with Syria ended in 1961.
explanation.definitionFit: An uproar is a noisy commotion or public disturbance, a kind of trouble.

clue.text: Wars caused by Marx's popular religion?

definitions.note: the drug that gave its name to the wars
Marx called religion this, so it describes religion rather than naming it

blocks.note: first meaning: the nineteenth-century wars between Britain and China over the drug trade
second meaning: Marx called religion the ... of the people

explanation.walkthrough: 'Popular' means of the people, pointing to Marx's phrase 'the opium of the people'.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain fought China in the Opium Wars over that narcotic trade, and Karl Marx described religion as the people's narcotic.

clue.text: There's a lot to be said for having a festival here

indicators.note: to be said means the word is spoken out loud rather than written

blocks.note: one's lot in life is one's fate

explanation.surface: Holding a festival in this place has a lot going for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There's a lot to be said for' is a stock phrase; break it up and 'a lot' is the fate you are given.
explanation.definitionFit: A fête is an outdoor festival or bazaar, often held to raise money for a church or school.

clue.text: Ran account into debt

indicators.note: into means put inside something else

blocks.note: being in the red means being in debt
AC is the abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: Someone let their bank account slide into debt.
explanation.walkthrough: Banks once printed overdrawn balances in red ink, hence red for debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Raced is the past tense of race, meaning went fast on foot, just like ran.

clue.text: Thrill to choice line out of poem

indicators.note: out of is read as being outside, so the line goes round the poem

blocks.note: elect as an adjective means chosen, select
RY is short for railway, a line
If— is Rudyard Kipling's famous poem

explanation.surface: A reader is thrilled by a fine line taken from a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of' looks like extraction; it means the railway line sits outside the poem.
explanation.definitionFit: To electrify an audience is to excite them intensely, a figurative jolt of electricity.

clue.text: A ridiculous means of getting into Brazil

definitions.text: A ridiculous means of getting into Brazil

blocks.note: surface reading: an absurd way of entering the South American country
setter's reading: the overkill tool proverbially used to crack a nut, and a Brazil is a nut

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'a sledgehammer to crack a nut' means using far too much force; a Brazil nut has a famously hard shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Cracking a Brazil nut with a huge heavy hammer is the proverbial example of ridiculous excess.
